messages:
Olivia: Thanks for the all-hands! Quick follow-ups on pricing/credits — can you clarify how short-term bursts (e.g., sudden PLG free-tier traffic) consume credits? Do bursts drain the daily bucket or a separate reserve? Also, how do rate limits interact for Dedicated customers?

Sam: Short answer — bursts first consume the customer's active credit bucket. We do have a temporary onboarding burst buffer for brand-new signups (first 24h) that eases immediate throttling. For Dedicated customers, committed capacity changes the billing shape (see @Elaine). We'll publish a clear doc with examples. :memo:

Elaine: For metered billing: consumed tokens are billed on usage; credits reduce the billed amount. If credits cover usage, invoice is reduced. Bursts taken from credits will decrement the balance. If credits run out, usage falls back to pay-as-you-go rates.

Marcus: To add — Dedicated customers with reserved capacity are billed via commit for baseline. Usage above commit is billed as overage (unless there's an overlay credit arrangement). Rate limits still apply at the API key/route level to protect shared infra.

Ashish: Technical note on rate limiting: enforcement is per route + API key. We use a smoothing window to allow micro-bursts (short spikes). Typical behavior: we permit token bursts up to a short window (configurable, default 5s) then enforce an average RPS. Hitting sustained >RPS will return 429. We're standardizing response headers to make this observable.

Olivia: Can you show an example of the headers apps will see?

Ashish: Sure — example headers devs will see in responses:

```http
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 512
X-RateLimit-Reset: 165
X-Credit-Balance: 12400
X-Model-Used: redwood-chat-medium-v1
```

Sam: Packaging roadmap note: next quarter we're prototyping per-route pricing tiers (small/medium/large routes) to better match request shapes. There's also an opt-in burst-pool for PLG/free-trial tiers that gives a temporary shared burst buffer to reduce early churn.

Elaine: Rollover/expiry: default credit expiry is 12 months from issue for self-serve accounts. Enterprise contracts can specify alternate terms. We'll add this to the FAQ.

Marcus: Sales reminder — we can negotiate rate-cap exemptions or custom burst SLAs in enterprise contracts, but they require security/compliance signoff. Use the legal + security template.

Olivia: If a customer gets a fallback to a smaller model during regional capacity issues, how is billing handled? Is it by requested model or served model?

Ashish: Billing is based on the actual model served. We also log fallback events and surface them in the Console under the route + timeframe so customers can reconcile cost/quality. We tag billing records with model_variant, region, and fallback_reason.

devrel-bot: Pinned: draft follow-up doc -> https://intranet.redwood/handbook/pricing/burst-models (will replace with final after edits).

Sam: Action items: @Ashish to add header + rate-limit examples to the docs, @Elaine to confirm expiry and top-up policies in the billing FAQ. We'll drop a short FAQ in #docs by EOW. :white_check_mark:

Elaine: Confirmed — I'll update the billing FAQ and the manual top-up process this week. Manual demo top-ups (e.g., +100k tokens for 48h) are supported today via Support; automation is on the backlog.

Olivia: Awesome, thanks everyone. One small ask — can we get an example FAQ blurb for engineers that explains "why I got 429 even though I still have credits"? That comes up in support.

Ashish: Draft blurb: "A 429 can mean you exceeded your configured rate (RPS) even if you have credit balance remaining. Credits pay for tokens consumed, but rate limits protect the serving runtime; please check X-RateLimit-* headers to see remaining capacity. If you need sustained high RPS, contact sales for dedicated commit or request a rate-cap review"

support-bot: Note: Support playbook ref: /playbooks/billing/429-rate-limits.md (internal).

Olivia: Perfect. Thanks — closing thread. :thumbsup:
